prompts.bruno: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: two independent RGBA layers for an existing WW1 top-down railway gun boss in HEAD-ON. Reference image is the existing engine/gun wagon, preserve its worn dark steel / olive brown painted raster detail, crisp fine dark outlines, rich mechanical texture, exact overhead perspective (NOT side-view, NOT isometric), elongated single-wagon silhouette, wheels, handrails, couplers. Make a horizontal sprite sheet with TWO equal full-height cells side by side, ample transparent gutter, each cell same coordinate registration 512x768. LEFT CELL: complete fixed locomotive/rail chassis with all wheels, deck, fuel/boiler/armor, gun mounting saddle, stationary recoil guides, an exposed detailed loading tray, ammunition hoist and rear breech platform; REMOVE the complete moving gun barrel and breech from this cell, fill the revealed mechanical surfaces naturally; do not leave a ghost barrel. RIGHT CELL: ONLY the moving long gun barrel with thick breech block and recuperator tube, aligned pointing vertically toward the TOP of the sheet, exactly centered x, base breech at 56% of cell height, muzzle at 8% of cell height. The gun must fit and look connected when right cell is overlaid onto left cell at identical center. No base, no wheels, no chassis, no second barrel in right cell, no smoke, muzzle flash or cast ground shadow. Keep gun length approx 52% of cell height, width approx 14% of cell width, fixed cradle visible around breech in left cell. Left cell gun pivot x50%,y56%. Canvas filled with genuine transparency, no backdrop, no text, labels or grid. Muted WW1 game artwork with no lighting/style downgrade, no neon, no cartoon. IMPORTANT: both layers separate and do not touch across cells; at least 20 pixels clear border. Bruno variant: German long naval cannon on coal-fired locomotive carriage. Preserve boiler and chimney in upper rear of carriage, iron cross discreetly on chassis, long narrower gun tube. Gun can be reoriented up to enable recoil animation; avoid covering the boiler excessively. Chassis itself remains recognizable as the provided train, not a generic tank.
